57716b28de8d5814.title: South Indian Bank aims 16% loan growth in FY27 amid West Asia war risks
57716b28de8d5814.summary: Private sector lender South Indian Bank is aiming for a 15-16 per cent credit growth in FY27, driven by the retail, agriculture and MSME (RAM) advances, a top official said on Friday. The RAM advances, which constitute 61 per cent of the book, are targeted to grow at a higher level of 17-18 per cent by the bank. "Our festive-season growth strategy is focused on the RAM segment, particularly retail lending and gold loans. In the latest July-September quarter, the bank's gross advances increased by 18.67 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,09,517 crore, up from Rs 92,286 crore in the year-ago period. 90f67291ceb91b50.title: India GDP to grow 7.1-7.3% in FY27 on private investment revival: Deloitte
90f67291ceb91b50.summary: The Indian economy is expected to grow by 7.1-7.3 per cent in the current fiscal, with a sustained revival in private investment providing an additional source of demand, Deloitte India said on Friday. However, geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices and trade disruptions pose risks to the growth outlook, it added. Deloitte India Economist Rumki Majumdar said over the past decade, India's growth has rested on resilient household spending and sustained investment push in public infrastructure. Businesses now have better connectivity, healthier balance sheets, and higher capacity utilisation, which strengthens the case for expansion. "The question is whether these conditions will encourage private investment to play a larger role in boosting growth in the coming years. Recent indicators offer grounds for optimism. Gross fixed capital formation grew by 11.9 per cent in the first quarter of FY 2026-27, its fastest expansion in four years," Majumdar said. Deloitte Economic Outlook

b3aeaf544c92ebab.title: FIFA chief Infantino apologises for World Cup row, fails to appease critics
b3aeaf544c92ebab.summary: Gianni Infantino gave an apology to the toughest critics who want to oust him as FIFA president but no new details or documents on issues that most concern them at a showdown meeting of the ruling council of soccer's governing body on Thursday. Infantino provided no documents about the $4.2 billion World Cup sell-off plan he launched and quickly dropped in July. Nor did he give details to explain the Folarin Balogun red-card case at the World Cup or how U.S. President Donald Trump intervened to help the national team forward. FIFA will, however, review whether to continue awarding the peace prize that was created to give to Trump last December. Infantino was pressed by European soccer officials for written evidence about his secretive private equity plan for the World Cup with investor Joshua Kushner, which provoked a global rift and the biggest crisis of his near 11-year presidency. He frustrated them further by asking for written questions, FIFA vice president Debbie Hewitt said
